_provenance.note: Field-by-field honesty tagging per project convention. REAL = sourced directly from Base Power's own 'Installation, Operation & Service Manual — Base Power DC Energy Storage System, Model 000515.XX.Y' (owner's manual PDF, pages 9-13: DC ESS Schematic, Technical Specifications, DC ESS Active Protective Functions). MOCKED = simulated/fabricated to populate the UI, using REAL thresholds/ranges as bounds where possible. This manual covers the battery module ONLY ('Core' in this project's taxonomy) — it does not describe inverter telemetry, so this file does not mock inverter (INV-xxxx) data.

real_spec_source.comms: Isolated CAN bus (CAN H / CAN L) between BMS Host Controller and pack; DC ESS communicates telemetry via CANbus, but comms is NOT required for safe operation (safety functions are local to the BMS/AFE/pyro fuse)
real_spec_source.aggregation: 1-4 units in series per site, vertically stackable to an aggregate 40 kWh

protective_functions.trigger: max cell temp > 65C AND charge/discharge current > 0.5A
min cell temp < 0C AND charge current > 0.5A
min cell temp < -30C AND discharge current > 0.5A

real_spec_source.critical_note: Every one of the manual's 9 documented protective functions ends in PYRO FUSE ACTIVATION — a one-time pyrotechnic disconnect, not a remote-resettable fault. A real BMS hard-fault on this hardware means the unit is physically dead and needs a truck roll + unit swap, never an 'AUTO_FIXABLE remote reset.' The existing Fleet Health mock's AUTO_FIXABLE/SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE/DISPATCH_NOW taxonomy is still reasonable for CAN/firmware/comms-layer soft faults (not in this manual), but any of these 9 named hard faults should route straight to DISPATCH_NOW / L4, never auto-remediated. See _provenance.taxonomy_note.

_provenance.taxonomy_note: This file distinguishes two fault families: (1) the 9 REAL, manual-documented BMS protective functions above — hard, physical, pyro-fuse-ending faults; and (2) MOCKED soft-layer faults (can_link_unreliable, fw_version_mismatch, install/commissioning issues) carried over from the existing Fleet Health mock, which are plausible CAN/comms-layer issues but are NOT described anywhere in this manual and remain pure invention, unchanged from before.
mocked_fields_per_unit: asset_id serial suffix, site address, firmware_version string, install_date — fabricated but formatted to match the manual's real 000515.XX.Y pattern
soc_pct, soh_pct — SOC calc exists on real hardware ('SOx calculation with shunt temp compensation' per BMS Host Controller block) but no real formula/values were in this manual; simulated
pack_voltage_v, pack_current_a, cell_voltage_min/max_v, cell_temp_min/max_c, case_temp_c, ambient_temp_c — simulated readings, bounded by the REAL spec ranges above

can_bus status, dropped_frames_per_min, bus_off_events_24h, max_allowable_charge/discharge_current_a — simulated; the manual confirms these concepts exist (CANbus telemetry, BMS reports max allowable charge/discharge current) but not real numeric values
protective_function_status per unit (nominal/warning/tripped) and pyro_fuse_state — simulated against the REAL trigger thresholds above
severity_hint (L0-L4) — this project's own invented mapping from protective-function state to the Field RCA severity ladder, not confirmed by Base

units.note: Matches the existing Fleet Health mock's COR-0092 case (thermal_or_safety_event, Escalated L0). Max cell temp 63.7C is 1.3C below the real 65C pyro trip with discharge current well above the 0.5A qualifying threshold — a genuine near-miss, not an invented number.

Matches the existing mock's COR-0071 case (true_hardware_defect, L4, Awaiting field visit). Once pyro_fuse_state is 'activated' the disconnect is physically irreversible per the manual — CAN telemetry goes dark because the pack is hard-isolated, so downstream fields read null/0, not stale data. This is a real, load-bearing distinction the taxonomy should encode: 'activated' can never be auto-fixed or remotely reset, only physically replaced.

0.519V cell imbalance at low SOC — weakest cell (2.462V) is 0.062V above the real 2.40V under-voltage pyro trip. A real BMS would derate max_allowable_discharge_current_a exactly like this to protect the weak cell before it ever reaches the hard trip; the derating concept is real (manual, Aggregation of Units section), the specific derate curve is our own invented approximation.

units.site: 22 Pecan Grove Dr, Round Rock TX
units.note: Cell/pack chemistry is healthy; this is a comms-layer fault only. can_link_unreliable is the pre-existing MOCKED soft-fault category, applied here to a Core unit for the first time (previously only modeled on inverters) — the manual confirms CAN is the real comms layer for the pack, and confirms 'communication is not necessary for safe operation,' i.e. a real CAN-degraded pack can still be electrically fine, exactly as modeled here.

units.site: 310 Live Oak St, Round Rock TX
units.note: 58.6A charge current during a fast top-off, 2.4A below the real 61A / 10s charge-overcurrent pyro trip. A real BMS would be expected to throttle max_allowable_charge_current_a well before this point; modeled here as a warning state precisely because it's close enough to be worth surfacing before it reaches the hard trip.
